thread:
frank: throwing this into the ring — our current fallback logs are enormous and noisy. what if we emit a tiny "short_circuit" event per degraded request (reason enum + route + short prompt_hash) and keep heavyweight traces sampled for internal forensics?

ada: short_circuit? I like the term. main concerns: privacy (prompt data), regulator requests, and customers accidentally relying on reasons in prod.

frank: agreed. public short_circuit payload = reason (coarse), product_route, prompt_hash_prefix (8 chars), model_tag, ts. no host/node ids. heavyweight traces (stack, node, cache state) stored internally only when sampled.

reza: sketch payload: ```json
{"evt":"short_circuit","cust":"cust_77","reason":"capacity_pressure","route":"chat-v2","phash":"9a7b4c1d","mv":"v2.3","ts":5167890123}
```

lin: sampling model? always emit short_circuit (tiny) but sample full trace at 0.2% baseline per-customer, auto-bump to 2% during anomalies, emergency gate to 10% with ops approval. also per-customer cap for short_circuit events (eg 1500/min).

ada: auditability: if a regulator asks for "all fallbacks" for a time window, sampling won't cut it. we need a deterministic replay path: store prompt_hash + model_snapshot ref in short_circuit events and keep raw prompts behind strict RBAC so we can replay whole set if legally required. public analytics only see hashes.

frank: exactly. keep public footprint minimal but maintain internal reconstructability. add an "audit_replay_kit" workflow for legal/ops requests.

reza: infra note: new kafka topic short_circuit.events with per-customer throttles and a circuit-breaker to collapse storms. config proto: ```yaml
topic: short_circuit.events
per_customer_max_per_min: 1500
trace_sample_rate: 0.002
anomaly_multiplier: 10
emergency_gate: requires_ops_approve
```

lin: UX for Console — customers get an aggregated "short circuit by reason" bar and a small "request audit replay" action (RBAC + legal). for those who opt-in (explicit account toggle) we can add an opt-in header `X-RW-Explain-Fallback: true` to include reason in responses. default: no reason in API.

ada: consent is key. Console copy must clearly state what is shared externally vs. kept internal. also add a per-account privacy toggle for richer telemetry & an operator override for 24h elevated sampling for debugging. log any operator override in audit trail.

frank: API debate — returning reason inline enables better graceful degrade client logic but leaks policy. proposal: do not return by default. provide opt-in header and require account-level consent. that way customer teams control whether their apps see reason.

reza: security checklist: validate prompt_hash scheme (collision risk), ensure no PII in any short_circuit fields, and add immutable audit logs for any replay access. also TTLs: compact events retained 90d, raw prompts retained 30d internal-only unless legal hold.

infra-bot: ticket INF-1702 created: "short_circuit events + trace sampling + consent toggle + audit replay kit" assigned to @reza and @lin.

lin: next steps: reza -> draft kafka schema & producer lib, frank -> write API opt-in header spec, ada -> draft Console UX copy and legal touchpoint, meet in 48h?

ada: I'll coordinate legal/privacy.

reza: will open WIP PR for schema tomorrow.

frank: one last thought — telemetry costs can explode during cascading incidents. ensure the producer has exponential backoff and a hard drop to preserve SLOs. pseudocode: `if incident_mode then sample_rate=min(max_rate, sample_rate*multiplier) else normal`.

lin: ack. add a soft cap on internal trace writes and emit a detection metric that triggers ops alerts when we hit the cap.

frank: perfect. aim: tiny public surface, deterministic replay path for audits, explicit customer consent for richer per-request signals. thanks all. :thumbsup:
